ai.principleDecides: The AI proposes and carries out, but the human decides. It never sends anything out of the house and never deletes.

terms.title: Terms and privacy
terms.intro: Tavle is an open source tool for Kanban and Scrum teams, run by Haij. This is the agreement between you and us when you use the edition we run. If you run the code yourself, only the licence applies.

what.title: What Tavle is
what.body: A tool for keeping a team's work visible: boards, cards, sprints and the numbers that can be computed from them. We make no promise that it fits the way you work; try the demo first.

account.title: Accounts and access
account.body: You get in by applying or being invited. We store your name, your email and your workspace's name, and use them to sign you in and to write to you about the service. Passwords are stored hashed, and you can add a passkey and two-factor. We sell nothing, and we do not send marketing you did not ask for.

yourData.title: Your data
yourData.body: Everything a workspace puts in belongs to the workspace. It can be downloaded as a spreadsheet and JSON with one click and deleted entirely again, audit trail included. We do not look at it unless you ask us for help, and we never pass it on.

ai.title: AI
ai.body: With a language model set up, the cards and sprints a person asks for help with are sent to the model provider. Who that is stands under Settings → AI and in the list of subprocessors. The model proposes; nothing is saved without a person saying yes.

leaving.title: Leaving
leaving.body: You can delete your workspace immediately, without writing to anyone and without waiting. The export is one click away and readable without Tavle. We keep no copy afterwards beyond the nightly encrypted backups, which roll off after 30 days.

availability.title: Running and guarantees
availability.body: Tavle is new, and there is no uptime guarantee. We look after your data with encrypted backups every night, but take an export now and then if the project matters. The service is provided as it is, without warranties beyond what the law requires.

license.title: Licence
license.body: The code is AGPL-3.0. You may use it, change it and run it yourself; if you change it and offer it to others over a network, your changes must be available too. What you write in the tool is not covered by the licence — that is yours.

demo.title: The demo
demo.body: A demo workspace is created without e-mail or sign-up and deleted entirely after 24 hours, account included. Do not put real personal data in it. We keep only the technical log data needed to keep the demo running.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Write to martin@vintherconsulting.dk. If you have found a security problem, SECURITY.md in the repository says how to report it; use that rather than an ordinary email.

help.title: Help
help.intro: Two things on this page: how the tool works, and how to make a board help the team. The second part is the important one.

boards.title: Boards
boards.body: A board is one team's work. When you create it you choose Kanban or Scrum and give it a key such as WEB, so cards are called WEB-1, WEB-2 and so on. Everyone in the workspace can see and work on every board.

kanban.title: Kanban
kanban.body: The columns are your flow: Backlog, Ready, In progress, Done to begin with, and you can add more under the board's settings. Put a WIP limit on the columns where the work happens. When a column fills up it changes colour, and that is the sign to finish something before starting more. The board can also split into horizontal swimlanes — by kind, theme, area or your own named lanes — under the board's settings.

scrum.title: Scrum
scrum.body: Cards sit in the backlog until you put them in a sprint. Plan the sprint under Backlog, pick the cards, and start it. The board shows only the running sprint. When you close it, the velocity is written down and the unfinished cards go back to the top of the backlog or into the next sprint. Future sprints can be laid ahead in one series under Roadmap, so features can be planned across them before the cards exist.

cards.title: Cards
cards.body: A card only needs a title to exist. Click the title to open it: here you set the assignee, estimate, priority, due date, acceptance criteria and checklist, and choose which feature the card is part of, or which area it belongs to, and write to each other in the comments. Everything saves immediately. A blocked card gets a red edge so it is not overlooked.

estimates.title: Estimation
estimates.body: A board can count in story points, in hours or in T-shirt sizes — choose under Settings → Estimation. Sizes and points are the same numbers, because a size is only a name for a weight (XS 1 · S 2 · M 3 · L 5 · XL 8 · XXL 13), so moving between them changes no sums. Hours are another scale, and there the tool shows a table of every estimate on the board and what it would become, with a conversion factor you can adjust. Nothing is written until you say yes, and the switch stands in the activity with an Undo button.

undo.title: Undo
undo.body: Every change stands in the activity of its card or item with an Undo button. Undo runs the opposite action through the same rules as everything else — if the world has moved on because the card was deleted or the feature closed, the tool says no instead of guessing. What was undone is struck through in the activity, and the undo itself is written down.

backlog.title: The backlog
backlog.body: The backlog is the ordered list of what the team does next, most important at the top. Drag the cards, or use the arrows. Select cards with the checkbox and put them in a sprint with one button. At the top of the list the level can switch: the epic backlog folds out to features and on to cards, the feature backlog to cards — and on a Scrum board the sprint panels can be shown or hidden, giving the list the whole width.

insight.title: Insight
insight.body: Every number is computed from what actually happened to the cards, never from an estimate. Kanban teams look at cards done per week, cycle time and cumulative flow. Scrum teams look at the burndown of the running sprint and the velocity of the closed ones.

team.title: The team
team.body: Invite colleagues under Settings → Workspace. You get a link you send yourself. If the person has no account, it is created through the link. Owners and admins can change the boards' columns, swimlanes, themes and areas, invite and remove members; everyone else can do everything else.

ai.title: The AI help
ai.body: The AI help lives where the work stands, and always follows the same law: it proposes, you rework and say yes — nothing is saved without you, everything it writes is marked in the activity and can be undone, and what it reads is treated as data, never as instructions. Set it up under Settings → AI: choose a provider and model for the workspace — a hosted model in the EU, or your own local one through Ollama. It can then finish writing a card and suggest splitting a big one (on the card's page), write the sprint's story (on the sprint's page), and lay a starting point for backlog and roadmap from your own description of the product — “Build a starting point” on the backlog and the breakdown, or AI start the moment a new board is created. The “Suggest” buttons draft a “Done when” on epics and features and a goal for the sprint; closing an epic or feature with open children, the close conversation arrives with a reasoned proposal for each of them; and “Draft a brief” writes a short overview when an epic is due for review. While you type a new card title, it quietly suggests where the card belongs, and says so if it looks like a card you already have. Without a model the buttons say so honestly, and everything else works.

data.title: Your data
data.body: Under Settings → Data the whole workspace can be downloaded as a spreadsheet and JSON with one click, and the owner can delete it entirely. It is your data, always.

structure.title: Epics, features, themes and areas
structure.body: The backlog has one hierarchy with three levels: an epic is a result the team can reach in one or two quarters, a feature is a releasable slice of it, a card is the smallest deliverable and fits in one sprint. All three have a kind, Business or Enabler. Overview and grouping are handled by two fields on each item: Theme answers why, Area answers where. Two tests decide where something belongs, and the tool enforces them: if it can be finished, it is in the hierarchy; if it can never be finished, it is a theme or an area. If it has exactly one parent, it is hierarchy; if it can belong to several at once, it is a category. The Breakdown tab draws the hierarchy as a chart: epics on top, features and cards below, and everything without a parent waits in the tray. Drag things into place, or use the menu on each card — and zoom out when you need the whole picture.

roadmap.title: Roadmap and overview
roadmap.body: The roadmap draws epics on a line of quarters, coloured by their first theme. Drag the bar: the middle moves the epic, the edges change its duration. An epic without a target quarter is not drawn; it is listed underneath. On a Scrum board the view can switch to features on sprints: lay sprints ahead, and put each feature where you expect to build it — unfold an epic to see its features drawn where their sprints lie. The overview shows where the open work sits by theme, area and kind, the enabler share as one number, and five measures of whether the structure holds: the share without a parent, epics for review, items without an area, the enabler share, and themes and areas nobody uses.

map.title: The story map
map.body: The story map is the team's wall: features as yellow notes across the top in the story's order (what the user does first stands at the left), the sprints (or the columns on a Kanban board) down the side, and every card in the cell where its feature and its sprint meet. The map's order is its own and leaves the backlog's priority alone. Features go up from the tray under the heading, are dragged into place or moved with the arrows, and come down again from the note's menu. Cards without a feature stand in a dashed column at the far right, so they cannot hide. Drag a card sideways to move it to another feature, up or down to put it in another sprint, and write a new card straight into a cell.

help.abcIntro: Ten rules for a team working on a board. They hold whatever tool you use.

0.title: Make the work visible
0.body: Everything the team works on is on the board. Not most of it, all of it. What is not on the board nobody can help with, and nobody can see how much is in progress.

1.title: Limit the work in progress
1.body: Put a limit on the columns where the work happens, and keep it. Ten things half done is worse than three things done. The limit is not a punishment, it is a conversation: what do we finish first?

2.title: Finish before you start
2.body: When a column is full, help with what is in progress instead of pulling a new card. It is the one principle that shortens the time from idea to something working.

3.title: Keep cards small
3.body: A card should be finishable in a day or two. If it cannot be, split it. Small cards flow, big cards get stuck, and a blocked big card is a week lost.

4.title: One owner per card
4.body: Several can help, but one person owns the card and knows where it stands. A card without an owner is a card nobody has.

5.title: Agree on what done means
5.body: Write in the description what must be true when the card is done. Tested? Shown to somebody? Live? If the team does not share the answer, Done is just a word.

6.title: Look at the flow, not at the people
6.body: The numbers are about the system: how long a card takes, where it piles up. They are not about who is fastest. A team that uses the numbers to point fingers stops writing honestly on the board.

7.title: A blocked card is a signal
7.body: Mark the card blocked at once and write what it is waiting for. Then whoever can unblock it can see it. A blocked card that just sits in In progress is the most expensive card on the board.

8.title: Have a rhythm
8.body: Scrum teams have sprints; Kanban teams have a fixed time when they look at the board together. The rhythm is what makes the team tidy up, talk about what is stuck and decide what is next.

9.title: Improve in small steps
9.body: After every sprint, or every other week, one question: what do we do differently? Pick one thing, do it, and look at the numbers. Big changes rarely survive a busy week; small ones do.

help.closing: The tool does not make the team good. The ten rules do, and the board is there so you can see whether you follow them.

symbols.title: The symbols
symbols.body: Every kind of thing has its own symbol, the same everywhere: in the backlog, on the card, on the story map, on the roadmap and on the board. A flag is an epic, a puzzle piece a feature, a note a card, a bug a bug, and a wrench enabler work. The symbol always carries its word when you hover it, and a page that uses the symbols explains them at the bottom.

doneWhen.title: Done when
doneWhen.placeholder: The condition that makes it done
doneWhen.aiDraft: The AI's draft — rework it and save it as yours.

page.reviewBody: This epic has been open for more than {days} days. Is it still a result the team is working towards, or has it become a theme?
page.deleteBody: {key} will be deleted. What is under it stays, without a parent.

children.features: {count, plural, =0 {No features yet} one {# feature} other {# features}}
children.noFeatures: No features yet. Create the first one that can be released on its own.
children.noStories: No cards yet. Add the first one below.

close.title: Close {key}
close.body: {count, plural, one {There is one open child} other {There are # open children}}. Nothing closes on its own: choose what happens to each.
close.openStories: {count, plural, one {# open card} other {# open cards}}

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.empty: No epics to draw yet. Give an epic a target quarter and it shows up here.
roadmap.unplanned: {count, plural, one {# epic without a target quarter} other {# epics without a target quarter}}
roadmap.unplannedHint: An epic without a target is not drawn. A roadmap that shows bars without an end is lying.
roadmap.counts: {features, plural, one {# feature} other {# features}} · {done} of {total} cards done
roadmap.noEpics: The board does not show epics, so there is no roadmap to draw. Switch epics on under Settings → Structure.
roadmap.noSprints: No open sprints. Create a run ahead so the features have a timeline to lie on.
roadmap.noPlanned: No features are planned yet. Pick a sprint on one below.

releases.title: Releases
releases.undated: {count, plural, one {# with no date} other {# with no date}}

care.title: What is the backlog waiting for?
care.body: What a product owner should decide before planning. Nothing here means nothing to decide.
care.summary: {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} waiting · {points} {unit, select, hours {hours} other {points}}

clear.title: The backlog is in order.
clear.body: Everything has a place, a “done when” and work under it. Nothing is waiting on a decision.

unplaced.title: Waiting for a place
unplaced.body: {count, plural, one {# feature or card does not belong to anything yet} other {# features and cards do not belong to anything yet}}. That is allowed — the tool never invents a container — but somebody has to decide where they belong, or that they should not.

noDoneWhen.title: Missing a “done when”
noDoneWhen.body: {count, plural, one {# epic or feature} other {# epics and features}} cannot be closed until somebody writes down when it is finished.

emptyFeature.title: Features with no work
emptyFeature.body: {count, plural, one {# feature has} other {# features have}} no cards under them. Either the breakdown is missing, or the promise is no longer current.

emptyEpic.title: Epics with no features
emptyEpic.body: {count, plural, one {# epic has} other {# epics have}} not been broken down yet. A goal with no road to it is hard to prioritise against.

review.title: Epics to revisit
review.body: {count, plural, one {# epic has} other {# epics have}} been open a long time without anyone confirming it is still a result you want.

unestimatedTop.title: Unweighed at the top
unestimatedTop.body: {count, plural, one {# of the top ten cards} other {# of the top ten cards}} has no estimate. You cannot plan what you have not weighed.

tooDeep.title: Deeper than you reach
tooDeep.body: There are {value} points ranked, and you finish about {of} per sprint. The bottom of the list is unlikely to happen — consider leaving it unordered.

overview.title: Backlog care
overview.distributionBody: {cards, plural, one {# open card} other {# open cards}} · {points} {unit, select, hours {hours} other {points}}

map.title: Story map
map.leadScrum: Features across the top in the story's order, the sprints down. Put features up from the tray, drag them into place, and drag a card sideways to another feature or up and down to another sprint.
map.leadKanban: Features across the top in the story's order, the board's columns down. Put features up from the tray, drag them into place, and drag a card sideways to another feature or up and down to another column.
map.noParentHint: {count, plural, =0 {No cards without a feature} one {# card without a feature} other {# cards without a feature}}
map.rowCounts: {cards, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} · {points} {unit, select, hours {hours} other {points}}
map.emptyTray: The map is empty. Click a feature in the tray to put it up.
map.empty: No features yet. Create a feature, and it can go up on the map.
map.hiddenCards: {count, plural, one {# card off the map} other {# cards off the map}}
map.hiddenHint: Pick a card — its feature goes up on the map
map.orderDrift: The order here differs from the backlog's ranking — maybe on purpose, maybe worth a look.
map.alignBacklog: Let the backlog follow the map
map.showClosedFeatures: {count, plural, =0 {Show closed features} one {Show # closed} other {Show # closed}}

map.showDoneCards: {count, plural, =0 {Show finished cards} one {Show # finished} other {Show # finished}}
map.noDone: There are no finished cards to show.

release.body: A release is what you deliver together. It cuts across sprints and is the map's horizontal band.
release.name: Name
release.dateHint: May be left blank — not every release has a date yet.
release.deleteBody: The band goes, the cards stay. They fall back into “Not in a release”, where you can place them again.

decompose.title: Breakdown
decompose.epicEmpty: No features yet. Write the first one below, or drag one here.
decompose.trayHint: Features and cards with no place in the breakdown. Drag them in — or out to here.
